overview: European companies, the struggle for supremacy (Bengal, Marathas, Carnatic, Mysore, Andhra/Nizam) and the Governors-General/Viceroys: 20 official questions (2008-2024). Governors-General is the heaviest leaf (8, in 5 years); the rest are mostly date and 'who' one-liners. Chronology of settlements/GGs and year-matching appear from 2019.

rights won after Bengal (duty-free trade in Awadh, 1765); natural targets: Plassey 1757, Buxar 1764, Diwani 1765
Velu Nachiyar and Mysore help; natural targets: three Carnatic wars, Wandiwash 1760, Dupleix vs Clive

traps.trap: [Cause swap] State annexed for another reason slipped into a Doctrine-of-Lapse list
traps.spot: Multi-select of annexed states including Awadh or Sindh
traps.fix: Lapse = Satara 1848, Jhansi 1853, Nagpur 1854; Awadh 1856 = misgovernment; Sindh 1843 = conquest
traps.pyq: Awadh and Sindh excluded → 'II, III and IV' [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#23]

traps.trap: Measure shifted to a GG of another era
traps.spot: Reform list for one GG with one later item
traps.fix: First universities 1857 = Canning, not Bentinck (sati 1829, thuggee, NWP settlement)

traps.trap: Policy credited to the wrong Viceroy of the same decade
traps.spot: Press, local government and famine measures with Lytton and Ripon
traps.fix: Lytton passed VPA 1878; Ripon repealed it 1882, Factory Act 1881, Famine Code 1883
traps.pyq: VPA → Lytton [group1-prelims-2010#4]; year match VPA 1878 / Famine Code 1883 [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#22]

traps.trap: Father and son of Mysore swapped
traps.spot: Hyder Ali and Tipu both offered, with a date in the stem
traps.fix: Hyder ruled to 1782; Tipu from 1782: 1780 alliance = Hyder; French embassies and navy = Tipu
traps.pyq: Embassies to France and navy → Tipu Sultan [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#23]

traps.trap: Earlier English visitor vs royal ambassador
traps.fix: Hawkins came 1608 as trader-captain; Sir Thomas Roe 1615-19 as James I's ambassador
Anchor on a sure neighbour: Bobbili 1757 = Plassey year; da Gama 1498

techniques.name: GG ladder
techniques.how: [Fixed order] Memorise the GG/Viceroy ladder with one policy each; chronology and policy questions become a lookup.

techniques.name: Policy-to-GG one-liners
techniques.how: Pair each doctrine/act with a single GG: Lapse-Dalhousie, Subsidiary Alliance-Wellesley, Permanent Settlement-Cornwallis, VPA-Lytton.
techniques.example: 'Doctrine of Lapse' → Dalhousie; Cornwallis, Ripon, Curzon fall [group1-prelims-2010#12]

techniques.name: Reason-of-annexation filter
techniques.how: In a list of annexed states, attach the reason to each: lapse, misrule, conquest; keep only the asked reason.
techniques.example: Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur = lapse; Awadh misrule; Sindh conquest → 'II, III and IV' [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#23]

techniques.name: First-in-region sequence
techniques.how: Keep each company's regional first: English east coast Masulipatnam 1611, Balasore 1633, Hugli 1651, Calcutta 1690.
techniques.example: First English factory in Bengal → Hughli 1651; Calcutta is later [group1-prelims-2012#138]

techniques.name: Treaty consequence chain
techniques.how: Link battle → treaty → right gained: Buxar 1764 → Allahabad 1765 → Diwani of Bengal and duty-free trade in Awadh.
techniques.example: 'After Bengal, duty-free trade in' → Nawab of Awadh [group1-prelims-2010#2]

checklist: Year options close together? Anchor on a known event of the same year.
For an annexation list, write the reason next to each state.
Policy question: recall the one GG tied to it, then check the decade.
Hyder or Tipu? Compare the date with 1782.
Reform-of-X lists: the odd one usually belongs to a later GG.
